hindi: Is Am Are ka matlab aur use
hinglishMeaning: Is = hai (third person), Am = hu (main ke saath), Are = ho/hain (tum/hum/ve)
rules: I + am = main + hu
He/She/It/Name + is = wo + hai
You/We/They + are = tum/hum/ve + ho/hai
examples: I am a student. (Main ek student hu.)
She is happy. (Wo khush hai.)
They are coming. (Ve aa rahe hain.)

hindi: Is Am Are ke saath ING form kab use kare
hinglishMeaning: Jab kaam abhi chal raha ho tab Is/Am/Are + ING use karo
rules: Is/Am/Are + V1+ING = abhi chal raha hai
Is + Ving = wo kar raha hai
Am + Ving = main kar raha hu
Are + Ving = tum/ve kar rahe ho/hain
examples: I am eating. (Main kha raha hu.)
She is studying. (Wo padh rahi hai.)
They are playing. (Ve khel rahe hain.)

hindi: Was Were ka matlab aur use
hinglishMeaning: Was = tha/thi (I/He/She/It ke saath), Were = the/thi (You/We/They ke saath)
rules: I/He/She/It + was = main/wo + tha/thi
You/We/They + were = tum/hum/ve + the/thi
Was/Were = past of is/am/are
examples: I was happy. (Main khush tha.)
They were late. (Ve late the.)
She was beautiful. (Wo sundar thi.)

hindi: Was Were ke saath ING form ka use
hinglishMeaning: Jab past mein koi kaam chal raha tha tab Was/Were + ING use karo
rules: Was/Were + V1+ING = us waqt chal raha tha
Was + Ving = wo kar raha tha
Were + Ving = ve kar rahe the
examples: I was eating. (Main kha raha tha.)
They were playing. (Ve khel rahe the.)
She was sleeping. (Wo so rahi thi.)

hindi: Do Does Did ka matlab aur use
hinglishMeaning: Do/Does = present ke questions/negatives, Did = past ke questions/negatives
rules: Do = present me I/You/We/They ke saath
Does = present me He/She/It ke saath
Did = past me sab ke saath
Do/Does/Did = helping verbs (questions aur negatives)
examples: Do you like coffee? (Kya tumhe coffee pasand hai?)
Does she speak English? (Kya wo English bolti hai?)
Did you come? (Kya tum aaye the?)

hindi: Habit rule - roz ka kaam batana
hinglishMeaning: Jo kaam roz ya regularly hota hai usme He/She/It ke saath V1+es lagao
rules: I/You/We/They + V1 = hum roz ye karte hain
He/She/It + V1+es/s = wo roz ye karta/karti hai
Negative: don't (I/You/We/They), doesn't (He/She/It)
Question: Do/Does + Subject + V1
examples: I eat rice every day. (Main roz chawal khata hu.)
She goes to school. (Wo school jaati hai.)
He doesn't smoke. (Wo cigarette nahi peeta.)

hindi: Past me kiya gaya kaam batana
hinglishMeaning: Past me kaam karne ke liye V2 use karo, negative/question me Did/Didn't ke saath V1
rules: All subjects + V2 = past me kiya
Positive: Subject + V2 (no helping verb)
Negative: didn't + V1
Question: Did + Subject + V1
examples: I ate rice. (Maine chawal khaye.)
She went to school. (Wo school gayi thi.)
He didn't come. (Wo nahi aaya.)

hinglishMeaning: Jab kaam ho chuka ho aur uska result abhi bhi relevant ho tab Have/Has + V3 use karo
rules: I/You/We/They + have + V3
He/She/It + has + V3
Meaning: kaam ho chuka hai, result abhi visible hai
Negative: haven't/hasn't + V3
examples: I have eaten. (Maine kha liya hai.)
She has come. (Wo aa chuki hai.)
They haven't paid. (Unhone fee nahi di hai.)

hinglishMeaning: Since = jab se (specific point), For = kitne samay se (duration)
rules: Since + specific point of time (since 2020, since Monday)
For + duration of time (for 2 years, for 3 hours)
Both used with Present Perfect and Present Perfect Continuous
examples: I have been living here since 2020. (Main 2020 se yahan reh raha hu.)
I have been studying for 2 hours. (Main 2 ghante se padh raha hu.)

hindi: Kaam shuru hua aur abhi bhi chal raha hai
hinglishMeaning: Jab kaam pehle shuru hua aur abhi bhi chal raha ho tab Have/Has + Been + ING use karo
rules: Subject + have/has + been + V1+ING
Since/For + time = kitne samay se chal raha hai
Negative: haven't/hasn't been + V1+ING
examples: I have been studying for 2 hours. (Main 2 ghante se padh raha hu.)
She has been crying since morning. (Wo subah se ro rahi hai.)

hindi: Do past events me pehle wala
hinglishMeaning: Jab past mein do kaam hue aur ek pehle wala batana ho tab Had + V3 use karo
rules: All subjects + had + V3
Pehle wala kaam = Had + V3
Baad wala kaam = Simple Past (V2)
Both past mein hue the, lekin ek pehle
examples: I had eaten before she came. (Maine kha liya tha wo aane se pehle.)
They had left when I arrived. (Ve nikal chuke the jab main pahuncha.)

hindi: Past mein kaam chal raha tha aur tab tak
hinglishMeaning: Past mein koi kaam chal raha tha aur doosra event aaya tab Had + Been + ING use karo
rules: All subjects + had + been + V1+ING
For/Since + time = kitne samay se chal raha tha
Past ka present perfect continuous
examples: I had been waiting for 2 hours when she came. (Wo aane tak main 2 ghante se wait kar raha tha.)

hinglishMeaning: Jo kaam pehle regularly hota tha par ab nahi hota usme Used To + V1 use karo
rules: Subject + used to + V1 = pehle ye karta tha
Negative: didn't use to + V1 (NOT: used to not)
Question: Did + Subject + use to + V1
DID aane par USED→USE
examples: I used to smoke. (Main pehle cigarette peeta tha.)
She used to love me. (Wo pehle mujhse pyaar karti thi.)
Did you use to smoke? (Kya tum pehle cigarette peete the?)

hindi: Can Could ka matlab aur use
hinglishMeaning: Can = abhi kar sakta hu, Could = pehle kar sakta tha, dono ke baad V1
rules: Can + V1 = abhi kar sakta hu (present ability/permission)
Could + V1 = pehle kar sakta tha (past ability)
Can/Could + V1 = request bhi
After Can/Could always V1 (no es/s/ed/ing)
examples: I can speak English. (Main English bol sakta hu.)
I could swim when I was 10. (Main 10 saal ki umar mein tair sakta tha.)
Can you help me? (Kya tum meri madad kar sakte ho?)

hinglishMeaning: Had+noun = khaya/piya, Had To+V1 = karna pada, Had+V3 = pehle kar chuka tha
rules: HAD + noun = past of have (kaam kiya: I had food)
HAD TO + V1 = majboori past mein (karna pada)
HAD + V3 = past perfect (do past events me pehle wala)
examples: I had breakfast. (Maine nashta kiya.)
I had to wake up early. (Mujhe jaldi uthna pada.)
I had eaten before she came. (Maine kha liya tha wo aane se pehle.)

hinglishMeaning: Will = 100% sure future, sab ke saath same form, baad mein V1
rules: All subjects + will + V1 = future mein karega
Will = 100% certainty
Negative: will not / won't + V1
Question: Will + Subject + V1
examples: I will come. (Main aaunga.)
India will win. (India jeetegi.)
Will you help me? (Kya tum meri madad karoge?)

hinglishMeaning: May = shayad hoga (achhe chances), Might = ho sakta hai (kam chances)
rules: May + V1 = high possibility (achhe chances)
Might + V1 = low possibility (kam chances)
Both mean future possibility, not certainty
Probability: Will > May > Might
examples: I may come tomorrow. (Shayad main kal aaunga.)
I might get a job. (Ho sakta hai mujhe job mil jaaye.)

hinglishMeaning: Shall = formal English, offers/suggestions mein (Shall I/We), documents mein
rules: Shall = formal/legal English mein use hota hai
Shall I/We = offer/suggestion (Kya main karu? Kya hum karein?)
In spoken English, WILL replaces SHALL almost everywhere
Documents/contracts mein Shall ka use
examples: Shall I help you? (Kya main madad karu?)
Shall we start? (Kya hum start karein?)
The tenant shall pay rent. (Kiraayedaar ko kiraaya dena hoga.)

topic: WILL BE / MAY BE / MIGHT BE
hinglishMeaning: MAYBE (ek word) = shayad, MAY BE (do words) = future possibility
rules: Will Be + No Action = future state (busy/late/happy)
May Be + No Action = future possibility state
Might Be + No Action = future low possibility state
BE ke baad: No Action Word, ING, ya V3 - sirf ye 3 rules
examples: I will be late. (Main late hunga.)
She may be busy. (Wo busy hogi shayad.)
He might be sleeping. (Wo so raha hoga shayad.)

topic: MUST HAVE / MAY HAVE / MIGHT HAVE
hindi: Past mein kya hua hoga guessing
hinglishMeaning: Past mein guess karna ho to Must Have=100%, May Have=high, Might Have=low chance
rules: Must Have + V3 = pakka kiya hoga (100% past certainty)
May Have + V3 = shayad kiya hoga (high past possibility)
Might Have + V3 = ho sakta hai kiya hoga (low past possibility)
Past ka probability scale: Must Have > May Have > Might Have
examples: He must have slept. (Wo pakka so gaya hoga.)
She may have forgotten. (Wo bhool gayi hogi shayad.)
They might have missed the train. (Ve train miss kar gaye honge shayad.)

hinglishMeaning: Jab tak doosra kaam hoga, pehla kaam ho chuka hoga - Will Have + V3
rules: Will Have + V3 = future mein kaam ho chuka hoga
Structure: By the time + Subject + V1/Vs, Subject + Will Have + V3
First event = By the time + Present, Second event = Will Have + V3
examples: By the time you come back, your car will have got repaired. (Jab tak tum wapas aaoge, car repair ho chuki hogi.)

topic: WILL BE + ING / MAY BE + ING / MUST BE + ING
hindi: Future mein kaam chal raha hoga
hinglishMeaning: Future mein kaam chal raha hoga batane ke liye Will/May/Might/Must Be + ING
rules: Will Be + ING = kar raha hoga (100% sure)
May Be + ING = shayad kar raha ho (high possibility)
Might Be + ING = ho sakta hai kar raha ho (low possibility)
Must Be + ING = pakka kar raha hoga (strong certainty)
examples: I will be studying at 2 PM. (Main 2 baje padh raha hunga.)
She may be cooking. (Wo shayad khana bana rahi hogi.)
She must be talking to Rahul. (Wo pakka Rahul se baat kar rahi hogi.)

hinglishMeaning: Will = sudden future, Is/Am/Are+ING = planned future (pehle se decide)
rules: IS/AM/ARE + V1+ING + Future Time = pre-planned future
WILL = sudden decision (abhi decide kiya)
IS/AM/ARE + ING = already decided before speaking
examples: I am getting married in March. (Main March mein shaadi kar raha hu.)
Papa is coming in the evening. (Papa shaam ko aa rahe hain.)
I am buying a car on 5th March. (Main 5 March ko car kharid raha hu.)

hindi: Going To aur About To ka difference
hinglishMeaning: Going To = karne wala hu (planned), About To = karne hi wala hu (abhi)
rules: Going To + V1 = karne wala hai (future intention, time remains)
About To + V1 = karne hi wala hai (immediate, almost now)
Going To = Gonna (informal spoken)
Was/Were + About To + V1 = karne wala tha (past)
examples: I am going to buy a car. (Main car kharidne wala hu.)
I am about to tell you something. (Main abhi tumhe kuch batane wala hu.)
I was about to call you. (Main tumhe call karne hi wala tha.)

topic: WOULD RATHER / IT IS HIGH TIME / I WISH
hinglishMeaning: V2 = past nahi bhi ho sakta - preference/advice/wish/imaginary mein
rules: Would Rather + Subject + V2 = main chahunga ki...
It is high time + Subject + V2 = ab waqt aa gaya hai ki...
I wish + Subject + V2 = kaash...
V2 does NOT always mean past - imaginary/wish/preference
examples: I would rather you spoke English. (Main chahunga ki tum English bolo.)
It is high time we started. (Ab GD shuru kar deni chahiye.)
I wish I knew the answer. (Kaash mujhe answer pata hota.)

hindi: Agar aisa hota to main aisa karta
hinglishMeaning: Agar aisa hota to aisa karta = If + V2, Would + V1 (imaginary/unreal)
rules: If + V2, Would + V1 = imaginary/unreal future
In Second Conditional, use WERE with everyone (I were, He were, She were)
Real Future: If + Present, Will + V1
Imaginary Future: If + V2, Would + V1
examples: If I got this job, I would work very hard. (Agar mujhe ye job mil jaati to main mehnat karta.)
If I won a lottery, I would buy a car. (Agar lottery lag jaati to car kharidta.)
If I were rich, I would buy a Ferrari. (Agar main ameer hota to Ferrari kharidta.)

hinglishMeaning: Zero=truth, First=real future, Second=imaginary, Third=past regret
rules: Zero: If + Present, Present (universal truth)
First: If + Present, Will + V1 (real future)
Second: If + V2, Would + V1 (imaginary future)
Third: If + Had + V3, Would Have + V3 (past regret)
examples: If you touch fire, you get burned. (Aag chhoge to jaloge hi.)
If you study, you will pass. (Padhoge to pass ho jaoge.)
If I had known, I would have come. (Agar pata hota to aa jaata.)

hinglishMeaning: Positive sentence ke baad negative tag, negative ke baad positive tag - always opposite
rules: Positive statement → Negative tag
Negative statement → Positive tag
I am → aren't I (exception)
Used to → didn't you (NOT usedn't you)
Always opposite - positive to negative, negative to positive
examples: You are coming, aren't you? (Tum aa rahe ho na?)
She isn't angry, is she? (Wo gussa nahi hai na?)
I am improving, aren't I? (Main improve ho raha hu na?)

topic: Neither/Nor, Either/Or, Neither Of, Either Of
hindi: Na ye na wo / Ya to ye ya wo
hinglishMeaning: Neither Of/Either Of = hamesha singular verb, Neither...Nor/Either...Or = verb subject after NOR/OR
rules: Neither...Nor = na ye na wo (donon nahi)
Either...Or = ya ye ya wo (ek to hoga)
Neither Of + singular verb (donon me se koi nahi)
Either Of + singular verb (donon me se ek)
Verb follows subject after NOR/OR
examples: She neither eats nor drinks. (Na wo khati hai na peeti hai.)
Neither of them knows me. (Donon me se koi mujhe nahi jaanta.)
Either of you can help me. (Tum dono me se koi ek meri help kar sakta hai.)

hindi: Bhi / Bhi nahi ke advanced forms
hinglishMeaning: Also=positive bhi, Either=negative bhi nahi, So+TV+Sub=main bhi, Neither+TV+Sub=main bhi nahi
rules: Also = bhi (positive only: I am also going)
Either = bhi nahi (negative only: I don't smoke either)
So + TV + Subject = main bhi (advanced positive: So am I)
Neither + TV + Subject = main bhi nahi (advanced negative: Neither am I)
Never use ALSO in negative sentences
examples: I am also coming. (Main bhi aa raha hu.)
I am not going either. (Main bhi nahi ja raha.)
I am happy. → So am I. (Main bhi.)
I am not happy. → Neither am I. (Main bhi nahi.)

topic: BE / BEING / BEEN - Forms of BE
hindi: BE ki 4 forms aur unka use
hinglishMeaning: Is/Am/Are→Being, Has/Have→Been, Will/Can→Be, Was/Were→alone
rules: V1: Be (will be, can be, should be)
V2: Was/Were (alone use)
V3: Been (has been, have been, had been)
V4: Being (is being, are being, am being)
Is/Am/Are + Being, Have/Has + Been, Will/Can/Should + Be
examples: Tea is being made. (Chai ban rahi hai.)
Tea has been made. (Chai ban gayi hai.)
Tea will be made. (Chai banegi.)

topic: Passive Voice - BE + V3 (Without Doer English)
hinglishMeaning: BE+V3 = doer nahi important, kaam pe zyada focus
rules: BE + V3 = Passive Voice (Without Doer English)
Is/Am/Are + V3 = habit passive (chai banti hai)
Is/Am/Are + Being + V3 = present continuous passive (chai ban rahi hai)
Was/Were + V3 = past passive (chai bani thi)
Was/Were + Being + V3 = past continuous passive (chai ban rahi thi)
Has/Have + Been + V3 = present perfect passive (chai ban gayi hai)
Will + Be + V3 = future passive (chai banegi)
Can/Should/May/Must + Be + V3 = modal passive
examples: Tea is made. (Chai banti hai.)
Tea is being made. (Chai ban rahi hai.)
Tea has been made. (Chai ban gayi hai.)
Tea was made. (Chai bani thi.)
Tea will be made. (Chai banegi.)

hinglishMeaning: Passive mein object pronoun subject form mein badal jaata hai (Me→I, Him→He)
rules: Me → I (I am being taught)
Him → He (He is being treated)
Her → She (She is being invited)
Us → We (We are being given)
Them → They (They are being called)
examples: Samir sir is teaching me. → I am being taught. (Mujhe padhaya ja raha hai.)
She has invited me. → I have been invited. (Mujhe invite kiya gaya hai.)

hinglishMeaning: LET→Be+V3, MAKE→Made+To+V1, Perfect Continuous→Getting+V3
rules: LET Passive: Let + Object + Be + V3 (Let the door be closed)
MAKE Passive: Subject + Be + Made + To + V1 (I am made to laugh)
Present Perfect Continuous Passive: Has/Have Been + Getting + V3
MAKE passive mein TO lagta hai (important difference)
examples: Let me close the door. → Let the door be closed. (Darwaza band ho jane do.)
She makes me laugh. → I am made to laugh. (Mujhe hasaya jata hai.)
My car has been getting repaired. (Meri car repair ho rahi hai.)

topic: Would Have / Could Have / Should Have / Must Have + BEEN
hinglishMeaning: Would/Could/Should/May/Must Have + BEEN → Been+NoAction ya Been+V3 (passive)
rules: Would Have Been + No Action (You should have been angry)
Would Have Been + V3 = passive (Tea should have been made)
BE → BEEN because these modals always take V3
Would Have Been + ING = not used here
examples: You should have been angry. (Tumhe gussa hona chahiye tha.)
Tea should have been made. (Chai ban jani chahiye thi.)
The project should have been submitted. (Project submit ho jana chahiye tha.)

hindi: A/An/The ka use situation ke hisaab se
hinglishMeaning: A/An = kaunsa nahi pata, The = dono pata hai, Uncountable mein A/An nahi
rules: A/An = listener doesn't know which one
The = speaker + listener both know which one
First mention = A/An, Already known = The
Uncountable (money/tea/water): no A/An
The + Uncountable = jab specific ho
Countable = A/An/The sab use ho sakte hain
examples: I have found a boy for you. (Ek ladka mila - listener nahi jaanta kaunsa)
Give me the chair. (Wo chair de do - dono jaante hain kaunsi)
The money you gave me. (Wo paise jo tumne diye the - specific)

hinglishMeaning: How Much = uncountable (kitna), How Many = countable (kitne)
rules: How Much + Uncountable = kitna (sugar/bread/money)
How Many + Countable = kitne (books/friends/teeth)
Bread = uncountable (How much bread, NOT How many bread)
Slices of bread = countable (How many slices)
examples: How much sugar is there? (Kitni sugar hai?)
How many books do you have? (Kitni books hain?)
How many teeth were there? (Kitne daant the?)

hinglishMeaning: Few/Little=na ke barabar, A Few/A Little=kaam chal jayega, Much/Many=negative, Any=zero
rules: Much = uncountable + negative (I don't have much time)
Many = countable + negative (I don't have many friends)
A Lot Of/Lots Of = positive + both countable/uncountable
Few = countable + almost none (negative feeling)
Little = uncountable + almost none (negative feeling)
A Few = countable + enough (positive feeling)
A Little = uncountable + enough (positive feeling)
Any = zero/none (negative/questions)
Some = positive (kuch hai)
examples: I have few friends. (Almost no friends - bad)
I have a few friends. (Enough friends - good)
I have little money. (Almost no money - bad)
I have a little money. (Enough money - okay)

hinglishMeaning: Although+But = galat, Though flexible hai, Even Though = strong contrast
rules: Although = but (contrast)
Though = but (more flexible, can come at end)
Even Though = strong but (strong contrast)
NEVER use Although + But together
Though can come at beginning, middle, or end
examples: Although he is rich, he doesn't spend money. (Wo ameer hai, phir bhi paisa nahi kharch karta.)
Even though it was raining heavily, we went outside. (Baarish bahut tez thi, phir bhi bahar gaye.)
I like him, though. (Main usse pasand karta hu, phir bhi.)

hindi: Jab tak / Agar nahi / Jab tak positive
hinglishMeaning: Until=time, Unless=if not (condition), As Long As=positive jab tak
rules: Until = time (jab tak/till a point of time)
Unless = condition (if not/agar nahi)
As Long As = positive condition (jab tak positive situation)
After Until/Unless: no WILL, no NOT, use V1
Unless already contains NOT
examples: I waited until 10 PM. (Main 10 baje tak wait kiya.)
Unless you study, you will fail. (Agar nahi padhe to fail ho jaoge.)
As long as I am alive, you don't need to worry. (Jab tak zinda hu, chinta mat karo.)

topic: AS Family - As Soon As / As Long As / As Much As
hinglishMeaning: As Soon As=jaise hi, As Long As=jab tak, As Much As=jitna, As Far As=jahan tak
rules: As Soon As = jaise hi (immediately after)
As Long As = jab tak (positive condition)
As Much As = jitna (quantity/degree)
As Well As = saath hi saath / along with
As Far As = jahan tak (as far as I know = jahan tak mujhe pata hai)
examples: As soon as the class starts, inform me. (Jaise hi class shuru ho, bata dena.)
As long as I am alive, don't worry. (Jab tak zinda hu, chinta mat karo.)
As far as I am concerned, this is correct. (Jahan tak mera manna hai, ye sahi hai.)

topic: As If / As Though / As Of Now / As It Is
hinglishMeaning: As If/Though=mano, As Of Now=filhaal, As It Is=jaisa hai waisa, As Usual=hamesha ki tarah
rules: As If = mano (imagination/comparison)
As Though = mano (same as As If)
As Of Now = filhaal/abhi ke liye
As It Is = jaisa hai waisa (jyon ka tyon)
As Usual = hamesha ki tarah
As + Adjective + As = jitna...utna (comparison)
examples: She looked at me as if she would eat me. (Wo mujhe aise dekh rahi thi mano kha jaayegi.)
As of now, let's call it a day. (Filhaal yahi samapt karte hain.)
Leave the project as it is. (Project ko jaisa hai waisa chhod do.)

hinglishMeaning: Would = past future, polite request, invitation, past habit, suggestion, imaginary
rules: Would = Past Future (I told her I would come)
Would you mind + V-ing = polite request
Would you like to + V1 = polite invitation
Would you like some + Noun = offering objects
Would + V1 = past habit (similar to used to)
Would + V1 = suggestion/advice (I would call him tomorrow)
If + Past, Would + V1 = imaginary (Second Conditional)
If + Had + V3, Would Have + V3 = past regret (Third Conditional)
examples: I told you that I would come. (Maine kaha tha ki main aaunga.)
Would you mind helping me? (Kya aap madad karne ka kasht karenge?)
Would you like to dance? (Kya aap dance karna chahengi?)
She would always tease me. (Wo mujhe hamesha chhedha karti thi.)

topic: Semi-Modal Verbs - Used To / Need / Dare
hinglishMeaning: Used To=past habit, Need Not=no zaroorat, Dare=himmat/courage
rules: Used To + V1 = past habit (positive only)
Need Not + V1 = no necessity (negative only, no TO)
Need To = action form (I need to go)
Dare + Subject + V1 = courage (question only)
Dare To = action form (Do you dare to come?)
DID aane par Used To → Use To
examples: I used to smoke. (Main pehle cigarette peeta tha.)
You need not worry. (Tumhe chinta karne ki zaroorat nahi hai.)
Dare you touch me? (Kya tum mein mujhe chhune ki himmat hai?)

topic: Short Forms - Gotta / Gonna / Wanna / Lemme
hinglishMeaning: Gotta=must, Gonna=future, Wanna=want, Lemme=let me - sirf informal mein
rules: Gotta = Got To = Need To/Must (I gotta go)
Gonna = Going To = future plan (I am gonna call you)
Wanna = Want To = desire (I wanna learn English)
Lemme = Let Me = permission (Lemme explain)
Informal only - NOT for interviews/formal communication
examples: I gotta study. (Mujhe padhna hai.)
She is gonna block you. (Wo tumhe block karne wali hai.)
I wanna talk to you. (Main tumse baat karna chahta hu.)
Lemme help you. (Mujhe tumhari madad karne do.)

hinglishMeaning: Negative questions = confirming ki nahi - Don't you know me?
rules: Full form: Time Word + Subject + Not + Action
Short form: Contraction + Subject + Action
Are not → Aren't you, Do not → Don't you
Pronunciation: Don't you → Doncha, Won't you → Woncha
examples: Don't you know me? (Kya tum mujhe nahi jaante?)
Aren't you coming? (Kya tum nahi aa rahe ho?)
Won't you come tomorrow? (Kya tum kal nahi aaoge?)

hindi: Special word pehle, phir helping verb
hinglishMeaning: Inversion mein special word pehle aata hai, phir helping verb, phir subject
rules: Normal: Subject + Time Word + Action
Inversion: Special Word + Time Word + Subject + Action
Special words: Never, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly, Barely, Little
Third Conditional Inversion: Had + Subject + V3 (remove IF)
If I had known → Had I known
examples: Never have I seen such a beautiful girl. (Maine itni sundar ladki kabhi nahi dekhi.)
Rarely does she talk to me. (Wo mujhse bahut kam baat karti hai.)
Had I known about your wedding, I would have come. (Agar mujhe pata hota to aa jaata.)

hinglishMeaning: 1 syllable→ER/EST, 2+ syllables→MORE/MOST, irregular memorize karo
rules: 1 Syllable: ER (comparative), EST (superlative)
2+ Syllables: MORE (comparative), MOST (superlative)
NEVER: More Smarter, Most Smartest (ER+MORE nahi)
Irregular: Good→Better→Best, Bad→Worse→Worst
Lucky→Luckier→Luckiest (Y→I change)
The + Comparative, The + Comparative = jitna...utna
examples: Tall→Taller→Tallest
Beautiful→More Beautiful→Most Beautiful
The sooner, the better. (Jitna jaldi utna behtar.)
Good→Better→Best, Bad→Worse→Worst

hindi: Formal connectors for GDs and interviews
hinglishMeaning: Moreover=iske alawa, Whereas=jabki, Nonetheless=phir bhi, However=haalaanki, So That=taaki
rules: Moreover = iske alawa (adding information)
Whereas = jabki (contrast)
Nonetheless = phir bhi (despite that)
However = haalaanki (but)
So That = taaki (purpose)
Used in formal writing, GDs, presentations
examples: Moreover, he is also intelligent. (Iske alawa wo intelligent bhi hai.)
He is rich, whereas his brother is poor. (Wo ameer hai, jabki uska bhai gareeb hai.)
It was raining. Nonetheless, we went outside. (Baarish ho rahi thi. Phir bhi bahar gaye.)

hinglishMeaning: Still=abhi bhi, No Longer=ab nahi (formal), Anymore=ab nahi (informal)
rules: Still = abhi bhi (continuing situation)
No Longer = ab nahi (was true before, not now)
Any More = ab nahi (same as no longer, negative style)
No Longer + Verb (positive style)
Don't + Verb + Anymore (negative style)
examples: I still live there. (Main abhi bhi wahan rehta hu.)
I no longer love you. (Main ab tumse pyaar nahi karta.)
I don't love you anymore. (Main ab tumse pyaar nahi karta.)

topic: I Want To / I Want + Object + To
hindi: Chahta hu / Chahta hu ki wo kare
hinglishMeaning: I want to+V1=khud karna, I want+Object+To+V1=kisi aur se karwana
rules: I want to + V1 = main karna chahta hu
I want + Object + To + V1 = main chahta hu ki wo kare
I don't want to + V1 = main nahi chahta karna
I don't want + Object + To + V1 = main nahi chahta ki wo kare
examples: I want to fly. (Main udna chahta hu.)
I want you to study. (Main chahta hu tum padho.)
I don't want you to go. (Main nahi chahta tum jaao.)

hinglishMeaning: It is he/she (NOT him/her) + Who + Verb = yahi hai jo...
rules: It is + He/She/Name + Who + Verb (NOT: It is him/her who)
Use subject form after It is: he, she, I, we
Past: It was + Subject + Who + Verb
It is he who knows. (NOT: It is him who knows)
examples: It is she who knows. (Yahi hai jo jaanti hai.)
It was he who helped me. (Yahi tha jisne madad ki.)
It is he who knows how to teach English. (Yahi hai jo English padhana jaanta hai.)

hinglishMeaning: The + Comparative, The + Comparative = jitna...utna... (donon comparative)
rules: The + Comparative, The + Comparative = jitna...utna...
Both parts use comparative degree
No verb needed in short form
Common pattern in spoken English
examples: The sooner, the better. (Jitna jaldi utna behtar.)
The taller, the better. (Jitna lamba utna achha.)
The cheaper, the better. (Jitna sasta utna achha.)

topic: Not To Speak Of / Let Alone
hinglishMeaning: Not to speak of = formal, Let alone = spoken - dono ka matlab 'ki baat to chhodo'
rules: Not to speak of = ki baat to chhodo (formal)
Let alone = ki baat to chhodo (spoken)
Used when second thing is even more impossible than first
Main sentence + let alone + bigger thing
examples: Not to speak of tea, they didn't even ask for water. (Chai ki baat to chhodo, paani tak nahi poocha.)
He can't even run 1 km, let alone a marathon. (1 km nahi daud sakta, marathon ki baat to chhodo.)

hinglishMeaning: There = astitva hona (hai/hain), There is no = nahi hai, Is there = kya hai
rules: There is + Singular = ek hai (astitva)
There are + Plural = multiple hain
There is no = nahi hai
Question: Is/Are + There + ...
Two There together: one=existence, one=place
examples: There is God. (Bhagwan hain.)
There is a problem. (Ek problem hai.)
Is there any problem? (Koi problem hai kya?)
There is no sugar there. (Wahan sugar nahi hai.)

hinglishMeaning: Gen-Z words = modern informal vocabulary for young people
rules: This food is bussin = ye food bahut tasty hai
He is a sigma = wo ekdum cool/intelligent hai
That movie was epic = wo movie bahut achhi thi
This song is a banger = ye song bahut achha hai
He has great rizz = usme bahut charm hai
No cap = sach mein / no lie
Her drip is amazing = uska outfit/style bahut achha hai
That outfit is fire = wo outfit bahut achha hai
examples: This food is bussin. (Ye food bahut tasty hai.)
No cap. (Sach mein.)
His drip is fire. (Uska style bahut achha hai.)

hindi: Kisi ko bolna ki wo kare
hinglishMeaning: Ask + Someone + To + V1 = kisi ko bolna ki wo kare
rules: Ask + Someone + To + V1 = kisi ko bolna/kehna ki wo kare
Past: Asked + Someone + To + V1
Used frequently in everyday English
examples: I stayed as long as he asked me to stay. (Main tab tak ruka jab tak usne mujhe rukne ko kaha.)
She asked me to help her. (Usne mujhse madad karne ko kaha.)

topic: Had Been vs Was/Were - Duration vs Particular Time
hindi: Had Been + ING aur Was/Were + ING ka difference
hinglishMeaning: Had Been+ING=duration (since/for), Was/Were+ING=particular time mein chal raha tha
rules: Had Been + ING + Since/For = past mein kaam chal raha tha (duration focus)
Was/Were + ING = past mein kaam chal raha tha (particular time focus)
Had Been + V3 = pehle wala kaam (past perfect)
Had Been + ING with since/for only
examples: I had been waiting for 2 hours. (Main 2 ghante se wait kar raha tha.)
I was waiting at 4 o'clock. (Main 4 baje wait kar raha tha.)
She had been teaching me since morning. (Wo subah se mujhe padha rahi thi.)

hinglishMeaning: Has/Have Been + Getting + V3 = past se chal raha hai (passive form)
rules: Has/Have Been + Getting + V3 = past se abhi tak chal raha hai (passive)
Getting acts as continuous marker in passive
Rarely used but appears in advanced grammar
examples: My car has been getting repaired since morning. (Subah se meri car repair ho rahi hai.)
The work has been getting done. (Kaam ho raha hai.)

topic: Would Rather / It Is High Time / I Wish (Revision)
hinglishMeaning: V2 = past nahi, unreal/imaginary/preference/wish/advice mein
rules: Would Rather + V2 = preference (main chahunga ki)
It is high time + V2 = ab waqt aa gaya hai
I wish + V2 = kaash
If + V2, Would + V1 = imaginary future
V2 in these = NOT past tense, = unreal/imaginary
examples: I would rather you spoke English. (Main chahunga ki tum English bolo.)
It is high time you told the truth. (Ab tumhe sach bata dena chahiye.)
I wish I knew the answer. (Kaash mujhe answer pata hota.)

hinglishMeaning: All past forms together for complete revision and understanding
rules: Simple Past: V2
Past Continuous: Was/Were + ING
Past Perfect: Had + V3
Past Perfect Continuous: Had + Been + ING
Used To: past habit
Had To: majboori past mein
Could/Could Not: past ability
Much vs Many vs A Lot Of revision
examples: I ate. (Maine khaya.)
I was eating. (Main kha raha tha.)
I had eaten. (Maine kha liya tha.)
I had been eating. (Main kha raha tha.)

topic: IS/AM/ARE TO vs HAVE TO vs WAS TO vs HAD TO
hindi: Karna hai / Karna padega / Karna tha / Karna pada
hinglishMeaning: Is To=order(karna hai), Have To=compulsion(karna padega), Was To=karna tha, Had To=karna pada
rules: Is/Am/Are To + V1 = karna hai (order/instruction)
Have To/Has To + V1 = karna padega (compulsion)
Was/Were To + V1 = karna tha (past order)
Had To + V1 = karna pada (past compulsion)
examples: You are to attend the meeting. (Tumhe meeting attend karna hai.)
You have to clean the toilet. (Tumhe toilet saaf karna padega.)
I was to attend the meeting. (Mujhe meeting attend karni thi.)
I had to leave early. (Mujhe jaldi nikalna pada.)

hinglishMeaning: Will=100%, May=high chance, Might=low chance, Shall=formal/offers
rules: Will = 100% certainty
May = high possibility
Might = low possibility
Shall = formal English / offers/suggestions
Will Be/May Be/Might Be = no action words
MAYBE (one word) = shayad, MAY BE (two words) = future possibility
examples: India will win. (India pakka jeetegi.)
I may come tomorrow. (Shayad kal aaunga.)
I might get a job. (Ho sakta hai job mil jaaye.)
Shall I help you? (Kya main madad karu?)

topic: MUST HAVE / MAY HAVE / MIGHT HAVE / WILL HAVE
hinglishMeaning: Must Have=pakka, May Have=shayad, Might Have=kam chances, Will Have=ho chuka hoga
rules: Must Have + V3 = past certainty (pakka kiya hoga)
May Have + V3 = past possibility (shayad kiya hoga)
Might Have + V3 = past low possibility (ho sakta hai)
Will Have + V3 = future completed (tab tak ho chuka hoga)
Go home/upstairs/inside/outside = no TO
examples: He must have slept. (Wo pakka so gaya hoga.)
She may have forgotten. (Wo bhool gayi hogi shayad.)
By the time you come, she will have left. (Tumhare aane tak wo ja chuki hogi.)
Go home (NOT: Go to home)

topic: WILL BE + ING / MAY BE + ING / MUST BE + ING
hinglishMeaning: BE ke baad sirf 3 cheezein: No Action, ING, ya V3 - 4th rule nahi
rules: Will Be + ING = kar raha hoga (100% sure ongoing)
May Be + ING = shayad kar raha ho (high possibility ongoing)
Might Be + ING = ho sakta hai kar raha ho (low possibility ongoing)
Must Be + ING = pakka kar raha hoga (strong guess ongoing)
BE ke 3 rules: No Action, ING, V3
examples: I will be studying at 2 PM. (2 baje main padh raha hunga.)
She may be cooking. (Wo shayad khana bana rahi hogi.)
She must be talking to Rahul. (Wo pakka Rahul se baat kar rahi hogi.)

topic: IS/AM/ARE in Future / Going To / About To
hinglishMeaning: Will=sudden, Is/Am/Are+ING=planned, Going To=intention, About To=immediate
rules: IS/AM/ARE + V1+ING + Future Time = pre-planned future
Going To + V1 = karne wala hai (intention)
About To + V1 = karne hi wala hai (immediate)
Going To = Gonna (informal)
Was/Were + About To + V1 = karne wala tha (past)
examples: I am getting married in March. (Main March mein shaadi kar raha hu.)
I am going to buy a car. (Main car kharidne wala hu.)
I am about to tell you something. (Main abhi kuch batane wala hu.)

topic: Second Conditional / Imaginary Future / V2 Non-Past
hinglishMeaning: V2 = past nahi bhi ho sakta - imaginary/preference/wish/advice mein
rules: If + V2, Would + V1 = imaginary/unreal future
Would Rather + V2 = preference
It is high time + V2 = advice
I wish + V2 = kaash
In Second Conditional: use WERE with everyone (I were, He were)
Real: If+Present, Will+V1 vs Imaginary: If+V2, Would+V1
examples: If I got this job, I would work hard. (Agar job mili to mehnat karta.)
If I were rich, I would buy a Ferrari. (Agar ameer hota to Ferrari kharidta.)
I wish I knew the answer. (Kaash mujhe answer pata hota.)

hinglishMeaning: Zero=truth, First=real future, Second=imaginary, Third=past regret
rules: Zero: If+Present, Present (universal truth)
First: If+Present, Will+V1 (real future)
Second: If+V2, Would+V1 (imaginary)
Third: If+Had+V3, Would Have+V3 (past regret)
Third Conditional: use WERE with everyone
If I had had = first HAD helping, second HAD = V3 of HAVE
examples: If you touch fire, you get burned. (Aag chhoge to jaloge.)
If you study, you will pass. (Padhoge to pass ho jaoge.)
If I had known, I would have come. (Agar pata hota to aa jaata.)

hinglishMeaning: Positive→Negative tag, Negative→Positive tag, always opposite
rules: Positive statement → Negative tag
Negative statement → Positive tag
I am → aren't I (exception)
Used to → didn't you
Will → won't, Can → can't, Have → haven't
Used To question tag → didn't you (NOT usedn't you)
examples: You are coming, aren't you? (Tum aa rahe ho na?)
You don't speak English, do you? (Tum English nahi bolte na?)
I am improving, aren't I? (Main improve ho raha hu na?)
You used to smoke, didn't you? (Tum pehle cigarette peete the na?)

topic: Neither/Nor, Either/Or, Neither Of, Either Of
hindi: Na ye na wo / Ya to ye ya wo
hinglishMeaning: Neither Of/Either Of=always singular, Neither...Nor/Either...Or=verb follows after NOR/OR
rules: Neither...Nor: verb follows subject after NOR
Either...Or: verb follows subject after OR
Neither Of: always singular verb
Either Of: always singular verb
Neither she nor I am going. (I→am)
Either Rahul or you are going. (You→are)
examples: She neither eats nor drinks. (Na wo khati hai na peeti hai.)
Neither of them knows me. (Donon me se koi mujhe nahi jaanta.)
Either of you can help me? (Tum dono me se koi meri help kar sakta hai?)

hinglishMeaning: Positive→Also/So+TV+Sub, Negative→Either/Neither+TV+Sub
rules: Also = bhi (positive only)
Either = bhi nahi (negative only, at end)
So + TV + Subject = main bhi (advanced positive)
Neither + TV + Subject = main bhi nahi (advanced negative)
ALSO never in negative sentences
examples: I am also coming. (Main bhi aa raha hu.)
I am not going either. (Main bhi nahi ja raha.)
I am happy. → So am I. (Main bhi.)
I am not happy. → Neither am I. (Main bhi nahi.)

hindi: BE ki forms aur passive voice
hinglishMeaning: BE+NoAction=state, BE+ING=action in progress, BE+V3=passive voice
rules: BE forms: Be(V1), Was/Were(V2), Been(V3), Being(V4)
Is/Am/Are + Being (present continuous passive)
Has/Have + Been (present perfect passive)
Will/Can/Should + Be (future/modal passive)
Was/Were alone (no other helping verb)
BE+V3 = Passive Voice / Without Doer English
examples: Tea is being made. (Chai ban rahi hai.)
Tea has been made. (Chai ban gayi hai.)
Tea will be made. (Chai banegi.)
Tea can be made. (Chai ban sakti hai.)

hindi: Habit passive aur object pronouns passive
hinglishMeaning: Is/Am/Are+V3=habit passive, Object pronoun→subject form in passive
rules: Habit Passive: Is/Am/Are + V3 (chai banti hai)
Past Passive: Was/Were + V3 (chai bani thi)
Me→I, Him→He, Her→She, Us→We, Them→They
Is/Am/Are + Being + V3 = present continuous passive
Has/Have + Been + V3 = present perfect passive
Negative: add NOT after helping verb
Question: helping verb comes first
examples: Samir sir is teaching me. → I am being taught. (Mujhe padhaya ja raha hai.)
People speak English here. → English is spoken here. (Yahan English boli jaati hai.)
It is said that ghosts live there. (Aisa kaha jaata hai ki wahan bhoot rehte hain.)

hinglishMeaning: LET→Be+V3, MAKE→Made+To+V1, Perfect Continuous→Getting+V3
rules: Present Perfect Continuous Passive: Has/Have Been + Getting + V3
LET Passive: Let + Object + Be + V3
MAKE Passive: Be + Made + To + V1 (TO lagta hai!)
MAKE: Make+Object+V1 (active) → Object+Is Made+To+V1 (passive)
examples: My car has been getting repaired since morning. (Subah se car repair ho rahi hai.)
Let me close the door. → Let the door be closed. (Darwaza band ho jane do.)
She makes me laugh. → I am made to laugh. (Mujhe hasaya jata hai.)

hinglishMeaning: Would/Could/Should/May/Must Have→BEEN (BE ki V3)→NoAction ya V3
rules: Would Have + V3 = karta agar chance milta
Could Have + V3 = kar sakta tha
Should Have + V3 = karna chahiye tha
Must Have + V3 = pakka kiya hoga
May Have + V3 = shayad kiya hoga
Will Have + V3 = tab tak ho chuka hoga
Been = BE ki V3 form (automatic after have)
Been + No Action OR Been + V3 (passive)
examples: You should have been angry. (Tumhe gussa hona chahiye tha.)
Tea should have been made. (Chai ban jani chahiye thi.)
The work could have been completed. (Kaam ho sakta tha.)

hinglishMeaning: A/An=unknown, The=known, How Much=uncountable, How Many=countable
rules: A/An = unknown thing, The = known/specific thing
Uncountable: no A/An, The only if specific
How Much = uncountable (kitna)
How Many = countable (kitne)
Bread = uncountable (How much bread)
Tooth→Teeth (irregular plural)
examples: I found a boy. (Ek ladka mila - kaunsa nahi pata.)
Give me the chair near the door. (Wo chair de do - dono jaante hain.)
How much bread do you want? (Kitni bread chahiye?)
How many teeth were there? (Kitne daant the?)

hinglishMeaning: Few/Little=na ke barabar, A Few/A Little=kaam chal jayega, Any=zero, Some=kuch hai
rules: Much = uncountable + negative (I don't have much time)
Many = countable + negative (I don't have many friends)
A Lot Of/Lots Of = positive + both (I have a lot of money)
Few = countable + almost none (negative feeling)
A Few = countable + enough (positive feeling)
Little = uncountable + almost none (negative)
A Little = uncountable + enough (positive)
Any = zero (negative/questions)
Some = positive (kuch hai)
examples: I have few friends. (Almost no friends - bad)
I have a few friends. (Enough friends - good)
I have little money. (Almost no money)
I have a little money. (Enough money)

hinglishMeaning: Although=but, Unless=if not, Until=time, As Long As=positive jab tak
rules: Although = But (contrast)
Though = But (flexible, can come at end)
Even Though = Strong But (strong contrast)
Until = Till a time (time)
Unless = If not (condition)
As Long As = Positive condition (jab tak)
After Until/Unless: no WILL, no NOT
Although + But = WRONG (never together)
examples: Although he is rich, he is unhappy. (Wo ameer hai, phir bhi dukhi hai.)
Unless you study, you will fail. (Agar nahi padhe to fail ho jaoge.)
As long as I am alive, don't worry. (Jab tak zinda hu, chinta mat karo.)

hinglishMeaning: As Soon As=jaise hi, As Long As=jab tak, As Much As=jitna, As Far As=jahan tak
rules: As Soon As = jaise hi
As Long As = jab tak (positive)
As Much As = jitna
As Well As = saath hi saath / along with
As Far As = jahan tak (As far as I know)
As If = mano (imagination)
As Though = mano (same as As If)
As Of Now = filhaal
As It Is = jaisa hai waisa
As Usual = hamesha ki tarah
As + Adj + As = jitna...utna
examples: As soon as the class starts, inform me. (Jaise hi class shuru ho, bata dena.)
As far as I am concerned, this is correct. (Jahan tak mera manna hai, ye sahi hai.)
As if she would eat me. (Mano wo mujhe kha jaayegi.)
The sooner, the better. (Jitna jaldi utna behtar.)

hinglishMeaning: Would = past future, polite request, invitation, past habit, suggestion, imaginary
rules: 1. Future in Past: I told her I would come
2. Request: Would you mind + V-ing?
3. Invitation: Would you like to + V1?
4. Object Offer: Would you like some + Noun?
5. Past Habit: Would + V1 (like used to)
6. Imaginary: If + V2, Would + V1
7. Impossible Past: If + Had + V3, Would Have + V3
8. Suggestion: I would like you to...
examples: Would you mind helping me? (Kya aap madad karne ka kasht karenge?)
Would you like to dance? (Kya aap dance karna chahengi?)
If I were rich, I would buy a Ferrari. (Agar ameer hota to Ferrari kharidta.)
I would call him tomorrow. (Meri baat mano to kal call karta.)

topic: Semi-Modal Verbs - Used To / Need / Dare
hinglishMeaning: Used To=past habit, Need Not=no zaroorat, Dare=himmat
rules: Used To + V1 = past habit (positive only)
Need Not + V1 = no necessity (negative only)
Need To = action form (I need to go)
Dare + Subject + V1 = courage (question)
Dare To = action form
DID aane par Used To→Use To
Need Not = no TO, no NEEDS
examples: I used to smoke. (Main pehle cigarette peeta tha.)
You need not worry. (Tumhe chinta karne ki zaroorat nahi.)
Dare you touch me? (Kya tum mein mujhe chhune ki himmat hai?)

hinglishMeaning: Gotta=must, Gonna=future, Wanna=want, Lemme=let me
rules: Gotta = Got To = Need To/Must
Gonna = Going To = future plan
Wanna = Want To = desire
Lemme = Let Me = permission
Informal only - NOT for interviews/formal
Extra: I'm, I'll, I've, He isn't
examples: I gotta study. (Mujhe padhna hai.)
She is gonna block you. (Wo tumhe block karne wali hai.)
I wanna learn English. (Main English seekhna chahta hu.)
Lemme explain. (Mujhe samjhane do.)

hinglishMeaning: Inversion = special word pehle, phir helping verb, phir subject
rules: Negative Questions: Don't you, Aren't you, Won't you, Can't you
Pronunciation: Don't you → Doncha, Won't you → Woncha
Inversion: Special Word + TV + Subject + Action
Never/Rarely/Seldom/Hardly/Barely/Little → inversion
Third Conditional Inversion: Had + Subject + V3 (remove IF)
examples: Don't you know me? (Kya tum mujhe nahi jaante?)
Never have I seen such a beautiful girl. (Maine itni sundar ladki kabhi nahi dekhi.)
Had I known, I would have come. (Agar mujhe pata hota to aa jaata.)

hinglishMeaning: 1 syllable→ER/EST, 2+→MORE/MOST, irregular memorize, never More+ER
rules: 1 Syllable: ER (comparative), EST (superlative)
2+ Syllables: MORE (comparative), MOST (superlative)
NEVER: More+ER or Most+EST
Irregular: Good→Better→Best, Bad→Worse→Worst, Little→Less→Least
Y→I before ER/EST (Lucky→Luckier→Luckiest)
The + Comparative, The + Comparative = jitna...utna
examples: Tall→Taller→Tallest
Beautiful→More Beautiful→Most Beautiful
The sooner, the better. (Jitna jaldi utna behtar.)
Good→Better→Best, Bad→Worse→Worst

hinglishMeaning: Moreover=iske alawa, Whereas=jabki, Nonetheless=phir bhi, However=haalaanki, So That=taaki
rules: Moreover = iske alawa
Whereas = jabki (contrast)
Nonetheless = phir bhi (despite)
However = haalaanki
So That = taaki (purpose)
Gen-Z vocabulary: bussin, sigma, drip, rizz, no cap, fire
examples: Moreover, he is also intelligent. (Iske alawa wo intelligent bhi hai.)
He is rich, whereas his brother is poor. (Wo ameer hai, jabki uska bhai gareeb hai.)
I study hard so that I can pass. (Main mehnat karta hu taaki pass ho jaun.)

hinglishMeaning: Still=abhi bhi, No Longer=ab nahi (formal), Anymore=ab nahi (informal)
rules: Also = bhi (positive)
Either = bhi nahi (negative, at end)
Still = abhi bhi (continuing)
No Longer = ab nahi (formal)
Any More = ab nahi (informal, negative)
No Longer = Don't...Anymore (same meaning, different style)
Vocabulary: Make a fuss of trifles, Give up, Quit
examples: I still live there. (Main abhi bhi wahan rehta hu.)
I no longer love you. (Main ab tumse pyaar nahi karta.)
I don't love you anymore. (Main ab tumse pyaar nahi karta.)

topic: VIP Rules - I Want To / It Is Who / The+Comparative
hinglishMeaning: I want to+V1=khud karna, I want+Obj+To+V1=kisi aur se, It is he/she who=yahi hai jo
rules: I want to + V1 = main karna chahta hu
I want + Object + To + V1 = main chahta hu ki wo kare
It is + Subject(he/she) + Who + Verb (NOT him/her)
The + Comparative, The + Comparative = jitna...utna
Presentation skills: standing, eye contact, hand movements
examples: I want you to study. (Main chahta hu tum padho.)
It is she who knows. (Yahi hai jo jaanti hai.)
The sooner, the better. (Jitna jaldi utna behtar.)

topic: Not To Speak Of / Let Alone + THERE (Existence)
hinglishMeaning: Not to speak of/Let alone=ki baat to chhodo, There=is/astitva hona
rules: Not to speak of = ki baat to chhodo (formal)
Let alone = ki baat to chhodo (spoken)
There is + Singular = hai (astitva)
There are + Plural = hain (astitva)
There is no = nahi hai
Question: Is/Are + There + ...
There is a will, there is a way. (Jahan chaah wahan raah.)
examples: Not to speak of tea, they didn't even ask for water. (Chai ki baat to chhodo, paani tak nahi poocha.)
He can't run 1 km, let alone a marathon. (1 km nahi daud sakta, marathon ki baat to chhodo.)
There is God. (Bhagwan hain.)
There is a way. (Ek raasta hai.)

hindi: Is Am Are ke saath 3rd form kab use kare
hinglishMeaning: Jab kaam khud nahi karte, kisi aur se hota hai tab is/am/are + V3 use karo
rules: Is/Am/Are + V3 = passive present (kiya jata hai)
Subject + is/am/are + verb 3rd form = kaam hota hai by someone else
examples: The work is done. (Kaam kiya jata hai.)
The letter is written. (Chithi likhi jaati hai.)
The food is cooked. (Khana pakaya jaata hai.)

hindi: Prepositions ke asli rules — logic se samjho
hinglishMeaning: Prepositions position ya direction batane ke words hain — logic se samjho, ratta nahi maro
rules: Prepositions = position (jagah) ya movement (chalna) batane ke words
Logic se samjho: koi cheez kahan hai ya kis taraf ja rahi hai
In = andar, On = upar touch karke, At = exact point
examples: The book is on the table. (Kitaab table ke upar hai.)
He is in the room. (Woh kamre mein hai.)
She is at the door. (Woh darwaaze pe hai.)

topic: Modal Verbs — Got To / Need To / Have To / Must / Want To
hindi: Majboori, zaroorat aur chahat ke beech farak
hinglishMeaning: Majboori (have to/must), zaroorat (need to), aur chahat (want to) ke beech farak samjho
rules: Got to = informal must (karna hi padega)
Need to = zaroorat hai (required)
Have to = majboori hai (must)
Must = strong obligation (bilkul karna hai)
Want to = chahat hai (desire, not obligation)
examples: I have to go. (Mujhe jaana padega — majboori.)
I need to study. (Mujhe padhna hai — zaroorat.)
I want to eat. (Mujhe khana hai — chahat.)
I must finish this. (Mujhe yeh khatam karna hi hai — strong.)

hindi: British aur American English mein farak
hinglishMeaning: British aur American English mein pronunciation, vocabulary aur spelling ka farak hota hai
rules: Pronunciation difference: colour (UK) vs color (US)
Vocabulary: lift (UK) vs elevator (US), lorry (UK) vs truck (US)
Usage: have got (UK) vs have (US)
examples: I am colouring (UK) vs I am coloring (US)
Take the lift (UK) vs Take the elevator (US)
I have got a car (UK) vs I have a car (US)

topic: Connector Words — As Soon As / As Long As / So That / Even Though
hinglishMeaning: Connector words do sentences ko jodte hain — har connector ka apna meaning aur use hai
rules: As soon as = jaise hi (immediately after)
As long as = jab tak (condition continues)
So that = taaki (purpose/reason)
Even though = bhale hi / chahe (contrast)
examples: I will call you as soon as I reach. (Main tumhe call karunga jaise hi pahunchunga.)
You can stay as long as you want. (Tum reh sakte ho jab tak chahte ho.)
I study hard so that I can pass. (Main mehnat se padhta hoon taaki pass ho jaaun.)
Even though it rained, we went out. (Bhale hi baarish hui, hum bahar gaye.)

hindi: In, On, At ke rules aur exceptions
hinglishMeaning: In = andar/lamba time, On = upar/din, At = exact point/ghanta
rules: In = enclosed space / long time (kamra, saal, mahina)
On = surface / specific day (table, Monday, wall)
At = exact point / specific time (door, 5 PM, station)
Exception: on Monday but at night, in the morning
examples: She lives in Delhi. (Woh Delhi mein rehti hai.)
The book is on the shelf. (Kitaab shelf par hai.)
I will meet you at 5 PM. (Main tumse 5 baje milunga.)
At night (not in night), in the morning (not at morning)

topic: TO + Verb 1st Form vs TO + Verb ING
hindi: Kab TO ke baad 1st form aur kab ING aata hai
hinglishMeaning: TO + 1st form = purpose, TO + ING = jab TO preposition ho (infinitive nahi)
rules: TO + Verb 1st form = purpose (taaki/karne ke liye)
TO + Verb ING = when TO is a preposition (not infinitive)
Look forward to meeting (NOT look forward to meet)
examples: I came to see you. (Main tumse milne aaya.)
I look forward to hearing from you. (Main tumhara jawab sunne ka intezaar kar raha hoon.)
She is used to working hard. (Woh mehnat karne ki aadi hai.)

topic: Second Form & HAVE — Completed vs Past Action
hindi: Completed action aur past action mein farak
hinglishMeaning: Past action = kab hua (2nd form), Completed = ho chuka (have + 3rd form)
rules: Verb 2nd form = past simple (pichhla kaam)
HAVE + V3 = completed action (kaam ho chuka hai)
I ate = maine khaya (past), I have eaten = maine kha liya hai (completed)
examples: I went to Delhi yesterday. (Main kal Delhi gaya — past action.)
I have finished my work. (Maine apna kaam khatam kar liya hai — completed.)
She wrote a letter. (Usne chithi likhi — past.)
She has written a letter. (Usne chithi likh li hai — completed.)

topic: Tell Me About Yourself — Self Introduction
hindi: Interview mein khud ko kaise introduce karein
hinglishMeaning: Interview mein pehle naam, phir background, skills aur goal — short aur relevant rakhna
rules: Structure: Name → Background → Skills → Goal
Keep it short (30-60 seconds)
Focus on relevant info, not personal details
examples: My name is Rahul. I am a computer science student with a passion for web development.
I have been learning DSA and building projects for the past 6 months.
My goal is to become a full-stack developer and work in a product-based company.

topic: Quantifiers — Much / Many / A Lot Of / Lots Of / Few / A Few / Little / A Little
hindi: Kitna aur kitni — quantity batane ke words
hinglishMeaning: Countable vs uncountable ke liye alag quantifiers — A laga toh positive, bina A ke negative feeling
rules: Much = uncountable (negative/question): not much water
Many = countable plural (negative/question): not many books
A lot of / Lots of = countable + uncountable (positive)
Few = countable (almost none — negative feeling)
A few = countable (some — positive feeling)
Little = uncountable (almost none — negative)
A little = uncountable (some — positive)
examples: I don't have much money. (Mere paas zyada paise nahi hain.)
I have many friends. (Mere paas bahut saare dost hain.)
I have a lot of time. (Mere paas bahut time hai.)
Few students passed. (Kuch students bhi pass nahi hue — negative.)
A few students passed. (Kuch students pass hue — positive.)
There is little hope. (Umeed bahut kam hai — negative.)
There is a little hope. (Thodi umeed hai — positive.)

hindi: Ek rule seekho, bahut saare sentences banao
hinglishMeaning: Ek rule pakdo, usse bahut saare sentences banao — pattern se seekho, ratta nahi
rules: Learn ONE rule at a time
Create MANY sentences with that rule
Expand simple sentences into complex ones
Practice pattern, not just rules
examples: Rule: Subject + Verb 1st form + Object → I eat rice. I drink water. She reads books.
Expand: I eat rice every day → I eat rice every day with my family at home.

hindi: To, Too, Into, Onto mein farak
hinglishMeaning: To = kahan jaana, Too = bahut/bhi, Into = andar jaana, Onto = upar jaana
rules: To = direction/destination (kisi jagah jaana)
Too = also/very (bhi/bahut)
Into = moving inside (andar jaana)
Onto = moving on top of (upar jaana)
examples: I am going to Delhi. (Main Delhi ja raha hoon.)
I am too tired. (Main bahut thak gaya hoon.)
She jumped into the pool. (Woh pool mein kood gayi.)
The cat jumped onto the table. (Billi table ke upar kood gayi.)

hindi: With aur By ke rules aur common mistakes
hinglishMeaning: With = saath/tool, By = dwara (passive) / paas / time tak
rules: With = saath mein (together/accompaniment/tool)
By = dwara (agent in passive) / paas mein (nearness) / by time (deadline)
Common mistake: 'by me' vs 'with me' in passive voice
examples: I am going with my friend. (Main apne dost ke saath ja raha hoon.)
The letter was written by me. (Chithi mere dwara likhi gayi.)
Come by 5 PM. (5 baje tak aa jaana.)
She cut the paper with scissors. (Usne kanchi se kaata.)

topic: ING Form — Five Rules of ING
hindi: ING form ke 5 rules kab use karein
hinglishMeaning: ING form 5 jagah use hoti hai — continuous, noun, preposition ke baad, certain verbs ke baad, aur adjective
rules: Rule 1: Continuous tense mein (I am eating)
Rule 2: As a noun / subject (Swimming is fun)
Rule 3: After prepositions (interested in learning)
Rule 4: After certain verbs (enjoy, avoid, finish + ING)
Rule 5: As adjective (interesting book)
examples: I am studying. (Main padh raha hoon — continuous.)
Swimming is good exercise. (Tairna achi exercise hai — noun.)
I am interested in reading. (Mujhe padhne mein interest hai — after preposition.)
I enjoy playing cricket. (Mujhe cricket khelna pasand hai — after enjoy.)
This is an interesting story. (Yeh ek interesting kahani hai — adjective.)

topic: Time Expressions — Since / Ever Since / Since When / Since Then
hinglishMeaning: Since = jab se start hua, Ever since = us waqt se ab tak continuous, Since when = kab se, Since then = uske baad se
rules: Since = jab se (starting point of time)
Ever since = us waqt se ab tak (continuous from past)
Since when = kab se (question — how long)
Since then = uske baad se (from that point onwards)
examples: I have been living here since 2020. (Main 2020 se yahan reh raha hoon.)
I have loved music ever since I was a child. (Mujhe bachpan se music pasand hai.)
Since when do you know him? (Tumhe kab se woh banda pata hai?)
He moved abroad and since then we haven't met. (Woh desh chhod gaya aur uske baad se hum nahi mile.)

topic: Perfect Continuous — Have Been / Has Been
hindi: Have been aur Has been kab use karein
hinglishMeaning: Have/has been + ING = kaam pichhli mein shuru hua aur abhi bhi chal raha hai
rules: Have been = I/You/We/They ke saath (kaam shuru hua aur abhi bhi chal raha hai)
Has been = He/She/It ke saath
Structure: Subject + have/has been + verb-ing + since/for
examples: I have been working here for 2 years. (Main 2 saal se yahan kaam kar raha hoon.)
She has been studying since morning. (Woh subah se padh rahi hai.)
They have been playing cricket for 3 hours. (Woh 3 ghante se cricket khel rahe hain.)

hindi: Be, Been, Being ka farak aur use
hinglishMeaning: BE = modal ke baad, BEEN = have/has ke baad, BEING = am/is/are ke baad + verb-ing
rules: BE = base form (after modals: should be, will be)
BEEN = past participle (after have/has/had: have been)
BEING = present participle (after am/is/are/was/were: is being)
examples: It should be done. (Yeh hona chahiye — BE after modal.)
I have been waiting. (Main wait kar raha tha — BEEN after have.)
He is being rude. (Woh rudeness dikha raha hai — BEING after is.)

topic: Modal + BE — Should Be / May Be / Might Be / Must Be
hindi: Modal verbs ke saath BE ka use
hinglishMeaning: Modal + BE = certainty ya possibility batana — should = chahiye, may = shayad, might = ho sakta, must = zaroor hoga
rules: Should be = hona chahiye (advice/expectation)
May be = shayad hai (possibility — uncertain)
Might be = ho sakta hai (less certain possibility)
Must be = hona hi chahiye (strong deduction/certainty)
examples: He should be here by now. (Woh ab tak yahan hona chahiye.)
She may be at home. (Woh shayad ghar pe hai.)
It might be raining. (Baarish ho sakti hai.)
You must be tired after such a long journey. (Itna lamba safar karke tum thak gaye hoge.)

hindi: Aadat batane ka rule — Subject + Verb 1st form
hinglishMeaning: Habit = 1st form use karo, DO chhupa hota hai, He/She/It ke saath S/ES lagao
rules: Habit = Subject + Verb 1st form (I eat, She goes)
Hidden DO concept: I eat = I DO eat (DO chhupa hota hai)
Third person: He/She/It + verb with S/ES/IES
examples: I wake up at 6 AM. (Main 6 baje uthta hoon — daily habit.)
She drinks tea every morning. (Woh har subah chai peeti hai.)
They play cricket on Sundays. (Woh Sundays ko cricket khelte hain.)

topic: Habit Questions — WHEN / WHAT TIME / HOW OFTEN
hindi: Aadat ke baare mein sawal kaise puchein
hinglishMeaning: Habit ke questions — When = kab, What time = kitne baje, How often = kitni baar
rules: WHEN = kab (general time)
WHAT TIME = kitne baje (exact time)
HOW OFTEN = kitni baar (frequency)
examples: When do you wake up? (Tum kab uthte ho?)
What time do you eat dinner? (Tum kitne baje dinner khaate ho?)
How often do you exercise? (Tum kitni baar exercise karte ho?)

topic: Present Simple for Future — Timetables & Scheduled Events
hindi: Present Simple future ke liye kab use karein
hinglishMeaning: Jab koi cheez scheduled ya fixed ho (train, meeting), toh present simple future ke liye use karo
rules: Present Simple = future mein scheduled/timetabled events ke liye
Bus, train, flight timings
Fixed appointments aur events
examples: The train leaves at 8 PM tonight. (Train aaj raat 8 baje chhootegi — scheduled.)
The meeting starts at 10 AM tomorrow. (Meeting kal 10 baje shuru hogi.)
My flight arrives at 6 AM. (Mera flight 6 baje pahunchega.)

topic: S / ES / IES — Third Person Singular Rules
hindi: He/She/It ke saath verb mein S/ES/IES lagana
hinglishMeaning: He/She/It ke saath verb mein S lagao, ending dekh ke ES ya IES bhi lagao
rules: General: verb + S (plays, walks, reads)
Ends in S/SH/CH/X/Z/O: verb + ES (watches, goes, fixes)
Ends in consonant + Y: Y changes to IES (studies, carries)
Ends in vowel + Y: just add S (plays, enjoys)
examples: He plays cricket. (Woh cricket khelta hai.)
She watches TV. (Woh TV dekhti hai — ES.)
He studies hard. (Woh mehnat se padhta hai — IES.)
She enjoys singing. (Woh gaana pasand karti hai — just S.)

topic: Conditional Structures — IF / WHAT IF / EVEN IF / AS IF
hinglishMeaning: IF = agar, WHAT IF = kya hoga agar, EVEN IF = chahe jo ho, AS IF = jaise ki (fake comparison)
rules: IF = agar (condition)
WHAT IF = kya hoga agar (hypothetical question)
EVEN IF = chahe jo bhi ho / bhale hi (regardless of condition)
AS IF = jaise ki (comparison — not real)
examples: If it rains, I will stay home. (Agar baarish hogi, main ghar rahunga.)
What if I fail? (Kya hoga agar main fail ho gaya?)
I will go even if it rains. (Main jaunga chahe baarish ho.)
He talks as if he knows everything. (Woh aise baat karta hai jaise sab kuch jaanta hai.)

topic: Special Spoken English Expressions & Advanced Speaking Patterns
hindi: Spoken English mein use hone wale special expressions
hinglishMeaning: Book wali English nahi, real life mein bole jaane wale expressions seekho
rules: Use natural expressions instead of textbook English
Learn phrases, not just individual words
Practice speaking in real-life situations
examples: I'm running late. (Main late ho raha hoon.)
It doesn't matter. (Koi baat nahi.)
I'll figure it out. (Main samajh jaunga.)
Let's call it a day. (Aaj ke liye bas karte hain.)

topic: Contrast Connectors — Although / Though / Even Though / Yet / Nonetheless
hinglishMeaning: Although = bhale hi (formal), Though = informal version, Even though = zyada emphasis, Yet = phir bhi, Nonetheless = iske baavjood
rules: Although = bhale hi (formal — sentence start ya middle)
Though = bhale hi (informal — sentence end mein bhi)
Even though = bhale hi (stronger than although — emphasis)
Yet = phir bhi (contrast in same sentence)
Nonetheless = fir bhi / iske baavjood (very formal)
examples: Although it rained, we went out. (Bhale hi baarish hui, hum bahar gaye.)
It was raining. We went out, though. (Baarish ho rahi thi. Hum bahar gaye, bhale hi.)
Even though I was tired, I finished the work. (Bhale hi main thak gaya tha, maine kaam khatam kiya.)
He is young, yet he is very wise. (Woh young hai, phir bhi bahut samajhdaar hai.)
It was difficult. Nonetheless, she succeeded. (Mushkil tha. Fir bhi, woh succeed ho gayi.)

hindi: Person, Persons, People, Peoples mein farak
hinglishMeaning: Person = 1, Persons = formal plural (2-3), People = general plural (most common), Peoples = alag communities
rules: Person = ek insaan (singular)
Persons = insaan (formal/legal plural — 2 ya 3)
People = log (general plural — most common)
Peoples = log/alag-alag communities (nation/race level)
examples: He is a good person. (Woh achi insaan hai.)
Missing persons report. (Gumshuda logon ki report — formal.)
Many people came to the party. (Bahut log party mein aaye.)
The peoples of Asia. (Asia ki alag-alag communities.)

hindi: Habit rule ka test aur common mistakes se recovery
hinglishMeaning: Common mistakes pehchano aur correct karo — galat bolna normal hai, improvement important hai
rules: Common mistake: I am go → Wrong. I go → Correct
Common mistake: She go → Wrong. She goes → Correct
Common mistake: He don't → Wrong. He doesn't → Correct
Error recovery = galat bolna normal hai, correction seekho
examples: I am go to school → I go to school.
She don't like tea → She doesn't like tea.
He play football → He plays football.
